sentences.en: When the long legal saga of WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange came to an end this summer, it marked the first time that the U.S.

sentences.en: In the weeks since, my colleague Charlie Savage has been thinking about what that conviction means for journalism and government accountability

sentences.en: It's Thursday, August 1St.

sentences.en: Charlie, Julian Assange, once a household name, really faded from public view over the last few years.
sentences.zh: 查理，朱利安·阿桑奇曾经是一个家喻户晓的名字，但在过去几年里，他确实淡出了公众视野。

sentences.en: You've covered him this entire time.

sentences.en: How were you thinking about him and his legacy when that guilty plea came down?
sentences.zh: 当那次认罪发生时，你是如何看待他及其遗产的？

sentences.en: So Julian Assange is one of the most interesting people of our times, and his saga is an extraordinarily complex and twisting one.
sentences.zh: 朱利安·阿桑奇是我们这个时代最有趣的人之一，他的传奇经历极其复杂且曲折。

sentences.en: Who he is or was, his status evolved over time.
sentences.zh: 他是谁，或者曾经是谁，他的身份随着时间而演变。

sentences.en: Was he the radical internet-based transparency extremist who facilitated the publication of leaked government U.S.
sentences.zh: 他是那个激进的、基于互联网的透明度极端分子吗？他促成了美国政府机密文件的发布，

sentences.en: documents bringing huge amounts of information to the public about how the world really worked?
sentences.zh: 向公众揭露了大量关于世界真实运作方式的信息？

sentences.en: Or is he the guy who published Democratic emails in 2016 that had been hacked by Russia as part of a covert intelligence operation to help Donald Trump win that election?
sentences.zh: 还是说他是那个在2016年发布了民主党邮件的人，而这些邮件是俄罗斯作为秘密情报行动的一部分窃取的，目的是帮助唐纳德·特朗普赢得那场选举？

sentences.en: And really, from my point of view, as someone who's interested in journalism and press freedoms,
sentences.zh: 说实话，从我作为一个关心新闻业和新闻自由的人的角度来看，

sentences.en: it doesn't really matter who he was because he became the first person in the history of the United States

sentences.en: to be convicted of violating the Espionage Act as someone who gathered and then disseminated to the public information that the government wanted kept secret.
sentences.zh: 因违反《间谍法》而被定罪的人，罪名是他收集并向公众传播了政府想要保密的信息。

sentences.en: And so his case ends with establishing a precedent that will be very important for investigative journalism, especially in the national security sphere, going forward.
sentences.zh: 所以他的案件最终确立了一个先例，这对未来的调查性新闻，特别是在国家安全领域，将非常重要。

sentences.en: Okay, I just want to unpack what you said.
sentences.zh: 好的，我想梳理一下你刚才说的话。

sentences.en: Many people may not view Assange as a journalist in the traditional sense, but because he pled guilty to a crime that involved disseminating government secrets to the public,
sentences.zh: 许多人可能并不认为阿桑奇是传统意义上的记者，但因为他承认了一项涉及向公众传播政府机密的罪名，

sentences.en: that word disseminating is key, it's something journalists do all the time, this case could affect journalists writ large.
sentences.zh: “传播”这个词是关键，这是记者一直在做的事情，这个案件可能会对广大记者产生影响。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And we're talking about government secrets in the realm of national security.
sentences.zh: 而且我们谈论的是国家安全领域的政府机密。

sentences.en: So we're talking about journalists' ability to report and really the public's ability to know what are arguably the government's most consequential activities.
sentences.zh: 所以我们谈论的是记者报道的能力，以及公众了解政府最重要活动的能力。

sentences.en: I mean, we're talking about how it wages war, where it sends weapons, how many civilians it kills in foreign countries,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们谈论的是它如何发动战争、向何处运送武器、在外国杀害了多少平民，

sentences.en: and what it does at home to police its own citizens in the name of national security.
sentences.zh: 以及它在国内以国家安全为名如何监管自己的公民。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: There's this whole category of extremely high-stakes information that sometimes voters really do need to know about for self-government to function.
sentences.zh: 存在着一整类极其高风险的信息，有时选民确实需要了解这些信息，以便自治能够正常运作。

sentences.en: And this step is the latest development in a longer story that goes back decades in how the government has been trying to use criminal law to protect information
sentences.zh: 而这一步是更长故事中的最新进展，这个故事可以追溯到几十年前，关于政府如何试图利用刑法来保护它

sentences.en: it does not want the public to know about.
sentences.zh: 不想让公众知道的信息。

sentences.en: So tell us that story of how we got here.
sentences.zh: 那么请告诉我们我们是如何走到这一步的故事。

sentences.en: Well, it starts with a law called the Espionage Act, and it was enacted during World War I to go after spies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这始于一部名为《间谍法》的法律，它是在第一次世界大战期间为了对付间谍而制定的。

sentences.en: And it makes it a crime for someone who does not have authorized access to government information about national security
sentences.zh: 它规定，任何未经授权获取国家安全相关政府信息的人，

sentences.en: to hold on to that information or to give it to someone else without authorization.
sentences.zh: 持有这些信息或未经授权将其提供给他人，即构成犯罪。

sentences.en: But the words of the law go beyond spying for a foreign government.
sentences.zh: 但法律的措辞不仅仅是为了对付外国政府的间谍。

sentences.en: On its face, this law could apply to ordinary people who are disseminating information not for the purpose of helping a foreign power, but for educating the public.
sentences.zh: 从表面上看，这项法律可以适用于普通人，他们传播信息不是为了帮助外国势力，而是为了教育公众。

sentences.en: Leakers.
sentences.zh: 泄密者。

sentences.en: Whistleblowers.
sentences.zh: 举报人。

sentences.en: Now, for most of the 20th century, the government did not try to use this law as a way to suppress leaks.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪的大部分时间里，政府并没有试图利用这项法律来压制泄密。

sentences.en: But things start to change in the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 但事情在21世纪开始发生变化。

sentences.en: Starting midway through the Bush administration, this is the period after the 9-11 attacks, there's all kinds of, you know, national security things going on,
sentences.zh: 从布什政府中期开始，也就是9·11袭击之后的时期，各种各样的国家安全事务正在发生，

sentences.en: all kinds of secret things going on that sometimes reporters find out about.
sentences.zh: 各种各样的秘密事情正在发生，记者有时会发现这些事情。

sentences.en: The Justice Department in this era starts to get tougher on leaks.
sentences.zh: 司法部在这一时期开始对泄密行为采取更强硬的态度。

sentences.en: They begin charging government officials with unauthorized disclosures of information under the Espionage Act and arresting them.
sentences.zh: 他们开始根据《间谍法》指控政府官员未经授权披露信息并逮捕他们。

sentences.en: And that new pivot against leakers continues through the Obama administration.
sentences.zh: 而这种针对泄密者的新转向在奥巴马政府时期仍在继续。

sentences.en: And so it's not really a partisan thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不是党派问题。

sentences.en: It is a Justice Department, national security, bureaucracy thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一个司法部、国家安全和官僚机构的问题。

sentences.en: And how are the leakers defending themselves against these charges?
sentences.zh: 那么泄密者是如何为自己辩护以对抗这些指控的呢？

sentences.en: The thing about the Espionage Act is that it is a pretty draconian law written for spies.
sentences.zh: 关于《间谍法》，它是一部为间谍编写的相当严苛的法律。

sentences.en: And so all that matters is, did you, without authorization,
sentences.zh: 所以唯一重要的是，你是否在未经授权的情况下，

sentences.en: acquire, retain, or disseminate national security information that could be used to harm the United States or aid a foreign adversary?
sentences.zh: 获取、保留或传播了可能被用于伤害美国或援助外国敌对势力的国家安全信息？

sentences.en: And so each act that fits in that category carries its own prison sentence of up to 10 years.
sentences.zh: 因此，每一项符合该类别的行为都有其最高10年的监禁刑期。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And the way the law is written, the defendant is not allowed, not allowed to say to the jury, you should acquit me because this disclosure was in the public intereSt.
sentences.zh: 而且按照法律的写法，被告不允许，不允许对陪审团说，你们应该判我无罪，因为这次披露是为了公共利益。

sentences.en: It's just not relevant whether you were trying to spy for a foreign power or educate the public.
sentences.zh: 你是否试图为外国势力从事间谍活动，还是为了教育公众，这根本不相关。

sentences.en: The question is just, did you mean to do it?
sentences.zh: 问题仅仅是，你是否有意这样做？

sentences.en: And if you did, you're guilty.
sentences.zh: 如果你有，你就犯了罪。

sentences.en: And so a pattern emerges.
sentences.zh: 于是出现了一种模式。

sentences.en: Because it's so hard to defend yourself against this charge and because the penalties are so steep, defendants start to plead out.
sentences.zh: 因为很难为自己辩护以对抗这种指控，而且惩罚非常严厉，被告开始选择认罪协议。

sentences.en: The government says, we'll make this case go away.
sentences.zh: 政府说，我们会让这个案子了结。

sentences.en: You go to prison for 18 months or two years.
sentences.zh: 你去坐牢18个月或两年。

sentences.en: And defendants over and over plead guilty because they don't want to take the risk of a very long sentence.
sentences.zh: 被告一次又一次地认罪，因为他们不想冒被判长期监禁的风险。

sentences.en: And these defendants at this point are still leakers, right?
sentences.zh: 而这些被告在这一点上仍然是泄密者，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, we're not yet talking about the government targeting people who publish the information from those leaks, like journalists.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们还没有谈到政府针对那些发布这些泄密信息的人，比如记者。

sentences.en: Yeah, there had not been any case in which the government tried to use the Espionage Act against people who are actually gathering and publishing information.
sentences.zh: 是的，此前没有任何案件是政府试图对那些实际收集和发布信息的人使用《间谍法》的。

sentences.en: Of course, the words of that statute going back generations on its face do seem to apply to newspapers and journalists who might do that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 当然，该法规的措辞几代人以来从表面上看似乎确实适用于可能做这类事情的报纸和记者。

sentences.en: But there had been a constitutional norm at a minimum, a consensus that applying the Espionage Act to journalistic acts would be a violation of the First Amendment.
sentences.zh: 但至少存在一种宪法规范，即一种共识，即对新闻行为适用《间谍法》将是对第一修正案的侵犯。

sentences.en: Congress should make no law impinging on the freedom of the press.
sentences.zh: 国会不得制定任何限制新闻自由的法律。

sentences.zh: 所以没有政府试图这样做。

sentences.zh: 据我们所知，他们是典型的举报人。

sentences.zh: 他是一位来自澳大利亚的计算机专家。

sentences.en: And we have a number of ways for them to get information to us.
sentences.zh: 我们有多种方式让他们把信息传给我们。

sentences.en: So we use this state-of-the-art encryption to bounce stuff around the internet, to hide trails.
sentences.zh: 所以我们使用这种最先进的加密技术在互联网上传输东西，以隐藏踪迹。

sentences.en: And the notion behind WikiLeaks is they're going to use technology and the growth of the internet to solicit and publish secret government documents
sentences.zh: 维基解密背后的理念是，他们将利用技术和互联网的发展来征集和发布秘密政府文件，

sentences.en: of public interest from anywhere in the world.

sentences.en: So information that organizations are spending economic effort into concealing, that's a really good signal that when the information gets out,

sentences.en: there's a hope of it doing some good.
sentences.zh: 有望产生一些积极的影响。

sentences.zh: 但事实证明，这个组织本身和作为领导者的阿桑奇还有更多东西可以提供。

sentences.en: And they start reaching out to major news organizations, including the New York Times,

sentences.zh: 所以他们与《纽约时报》和其他新闻机构合作，最终形成了这场信息喷泉。

sentences.zh: 维基解密再次泄密。

sentences.zh: 但是……
